recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Handle any eventual FHIR-54887 organizer/grouping text as a separate later R6 decision rather than reopening FHIR-16825.
issue_request: FHIR-16825 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3 by OO. It reported that Observation.component cannot model complex, inter-related findings and asked whether Observation.hasMember should be used; the resolution states that components do not nest recursively, hasMember is used for such complex findings, and panel/battery wording should be clarified as an example.
initial_application: The historical application appears in git-svn commit 69761b715e5c64e5f02da9d3cab64b40f1b00d1b, titled GF#16495, GF#16733, GF#16825. That commit changed the Observation grouping note from grouping related observations as a panel or battery to grouping them such as for a panel or battery, matching the Jira resolution. No prior combined-branch commit carried Issue-Reconcile-Key: FHIR-16825.
additional_context: Observation is active current-build source via source/fhir.ini and normative from 4.0.0. Current hasMember and component definitions, plus the Observation Grouping narrative, already distinguish independently meaningful related observations from inseparable components and explicitly allow nested grouping through hasMember. Later FHIR-51724 resolved No Change because the current text already distinguishes hasMember and component. FHIR-54887 is a later Triaged R6 grouping/organizer proposal and was treated as background rather than a final superseding decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active current source already conveys the FHIR-16825 rule and there is no final later decision showing a defect in that application.

related_jiras.note: Later Resolved - No Change issue found the current Observation.component and Observation.hasMember guidance already sufficiently clear.

Later Triaged R6 grouping/organizer proposal may revise related text but is not final enough to supersede this Published STU3 audit.
